### Observed differences

- The always-executed block A20, A21, A22, A24 and A25 (observed in all 200 traces in both windows) reversed its order relative to the segment A29 → A33: earlier each block activity preceded A29 in about 97–99 in 100 traces (and preceded A33 similarly), while in the later window A29 and A33 each precede the block activities in about 97–99 in 100. The same reversal holds against the optional A23, A27 and A28 (for example A20 before A27 in about 23 in 100 traces earlier, A27 before A20 in about 25 in 100 later). Mean relative positions moved from about 0.40 to about 0.65 for the block, from about 0.49 to 0.38 for A29 and from about 0.67 to 0.56 for A33. [REL017, REL019, REL020, REL027, REL029, REL034, REL038, POS004, POS009, POS013, POS014]
- The optional activities A19, A23, A26, A27 and A28 (each in roughly 18–27 in 100 traces in both windows) moved from after A33 to before A29: earlier about 90–98 in 100 of each one's outgoing transitions went to A34, in the later window about 90–93 in 100 go to A29. A33's outgoing transitions switched from about 97 in 100 to these five earlier to about 96 in 100 to the block later; A44's switched from about 78 in 100 to the block earlier to about 94 in 100 to the optional five later, now mostly at distance 1. Their mean relative positions moved from about 0.68–0.71 to about 0.35–0.37. [DIR005, DIR009, DIR013, DIR014, DIR015, DIR016, LAG011, LAG024, LAG027, POS003, POS011]
- Adjacency within five steps matches this swap: A21 or A22 reached A29 within five steps in about 195 of 200 traces earlier and in 1–2 traces later; A33 reached A20 within five steps in about 193 of 200 later versus 1 earlier; A20 reached A34 within five steps in about 195 of 200 later versus 1 earlier; the direct distance-1 links from A33 to A19, A23, A27 and A28 (34–46 traces each) disappeared, and direct distance-1 links from A44 to A19, A26 and A27 (35–50 traces each) appeared. [LAG013, LAG014, LAG015, LAG019, LAG020, LAG021, LAG022, LAG023, LAG024, LAG027, LAG028]
- A06 became much more frequent and much earlier: it appeared in about 17 in 100 traces in the earlier window (33 of 200) versus about 72 in 100 later (143 of 200), with its mean relative position moving from about 0.51 to about 0.18. [OCC002, POS001]
- A06 was rewired into the early sequence: earlier A14 led directly to A15 in about 87 in 100 of its outgoing transitions and A06's own transitions were spread over many targets (none above about 18 in 100); in the later window A14 leads to A06 in about 67 in 100 (about 2 in 100 earlier), A06 leads to A15 in about 89 in 100 (about 12 in 100 earlier), A06 follows A14 at distance 1 in about 96 in 100 of later co-occurrences, and the A14→A15 distance shifted from mostly one step (about 41 in 100) to mostly two steps (about 37 in 100). [DIR002, DIR004, LAG003, LAG004]
- A04 became rarer: about 19 in 100 traces earlier (37 of 200) versus about 6 in 100 later (12 of 200). [OCC001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the order of activities in the middle of the process was rearranged. In the earlier window, the always-executed activities A20, A21, A22, A24 and A25 ran before the segment A29 → A33, and the optional activities A19, A23, A26, A27 and A28 ran after A33, leading directly to A34; in the later window the two groups sit on opposite sides of that segment — A29 and A33 now precede the block, the optional five run between A44 and A29 and lead to A29 rather than to A34, and A33 leads to the block rather than to the optional five. [REL019, REL020, REL027, DIR005, DIR013, DIR015, DIR016, LAG013, LAG020]

The support is direct and consistent: order relations between activities that appear in all 200 traces of both windows reversed almost completely, successor profiles changed exactly at the junctions the rearrangement predicts (A33, A44 and the optional five), and adjacency within five steps appeared and disappeared where the swap predicts; the 105 qualifying items are roughly ninety times the number expected without a change (about 1), so chance sampling cannot account for the pattern as a whole. [screening, REL019, DIR015, LAG014]

The evidence cannot rule out that the two windows sample two process variants in different proportions rather than a modification applied within cases, and it cannot resolve the internal order within each group; the many agreeing items also largely describe this one rearrangement rather than independent confirmations. [REL019, DIR015]

Other differences:
- A06 became a standard early step: participation rose from about 17 to about 72 in 100 traces, its mean relative position moved from about 0.51 to about 0.18, and the earlier mostly direct A14 → A15 edge now usually runs A14 → A06 → A15 (A14 to A06 in about 67 in 100 of its outgoing transitions versus about 2 in 100 earlier; A06 to A15 about 89 in 100 versus about 12 in 100 earlier). [OCC002, POS001, DIR002, DIR004, LAG003, LAG004]
- A04 was observed in about 19 in 100 traces earlier versus about 6 in 100 later. [OCC001]
